scope: Experimental held-out BRISC segmentation validation; not clinical validation

training.model: MONAI compact 2D U-Net with linear logit head
training.loss: per-image background/foreground balanced BCE plus foreground Dice
training.selection_metric: validation macro mean across three tumor-type Dice values

visual_review: Fixed validation examples generally show correct localization and close overlap. Glioma commonly under-segments. Worst-case examples include complete misses, localization errors, and disconnected false-positive regions in every category.
limitations: No prospective clinical evaluation or clinician-validated deployment study was performed.
All reported segmentation metrics are from BRISC internal validation.
Glioma mean Dice is quantified at 0.6090, with 60/204 cases below Dice 0.50 and 12 zero-Dice cases; the limitation remains unresolved.
The sealed BRISC test partition was not accessed.

segmentation_validation_consolidation.scope: Consolidated visual, failure-mode, agreement, uncertainty, and reproducibility evidence for the 680-image BRISC internal segmentation validation partition; not clinical validation

failure_modes.population: 83 BRISC internal-validation cases with hard-mask Dice below 0.50
failure_modes.interpretation: Fragmented predictions and disconnected false-positive components are the dominant cross-category topology signals among weak cases.

classifier_segmenter_agreement.interpretation: Correct tumor-type classification does not imply reliable spatial segmentation.

uncertainty_signals.finding: Zero-Dice cases are confident spatial errors rather than globally uncertain cases. Classifier confidence cannot serve as a segmentation-reliability proxy.

tumor_type_confound.statement: The extreme-group confidence comparison is not tumor-type-controlled.
tumor_type_confound.key_imbalance: 12/17 zero-Dice cases are glioma; 15/20 highest-Dice cases are meningioma.

falsified_hypotheses.hypothesis: Zero-Dice predictions show a consistent skull-base positional bias.
falsified_hypotheses.interpretation: The errors are spatially heterogeneous, with only a modest lower-half shift; the observed four-case visual cluster did not hold across all 17.
falsified_hypotheses.predeclared_support_rule: At least 70% of zero-Dice centroids below the midline plus median lower-half fraction >=0.70, or at least 70% of centroids below y=0.60, or median lower-third fraction >=0.50

training_time_git_head.explicit_limitation: The exact training-time Git HEAD was not recorded. Commit 67ef814 is the source-equivalent commit, not a proven launch-time commit.

current_runtime_probe.scope: Two repeated synthetic forward/backward/AdamW/AMP steps on the current GPU runtime; no project image or accepted checkpoint was trained

specific_unenforced_or_environment_sensi.operations: CUDA Conv2d and ConvTranspose2d forward/backward through cuDNN
specific_unenforced_or_environment_sensi.reason: cuDNN deterministic mode was enabled, but the original run did not enable PyTorch's global deterministic-algorithm guard. An unsupported nondeterministic path would not have failed closed.

specific_unenforced_or_environment_sensi.operations: InstanceNorm2d, Dice/BCE losses, and CUDA gradient reductions
specific_unenforced_or_environment_sensi.reason: Parallel floating-point reduction order and kernel implementation can change across CUDA, cuDNN, PyTorch, driver, or GPU versions. The current runtime probe passes, but cross-runtime bitwise identity is not guaranteed.

specific_unenforced_or_environment_sensi.operations: CUDA AdamW update with AMP FP16 forward and GradScaler
specific_unenforced_or_environment_sensi.reason: FP16 rounding and overflow decisions can amplify small runtime-level differences. Early stopping and top-3 selection can then follow a different path even with the same seed.
CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG and TF32 policy were not explicitly recorded by the training run. The model path is convolution-heavy, but the environment contract is incomplete.
